proves: the three fields that travel with a background picture - repeat, size and position - reach the painter. Before this fixture's commit only the source did: draw_image_sized stretched the picture to the box and said so in a comment, so repeat and no-repeat drew the same picture and Cover and Contain were both the box.
checkable: 392x56, six 56x40 cells at y=8..47, at x=8, 72, 136, 200, 264 and 328, each white behind an 8x4 tile drawn at a size. Read three rows, y=12, 30 and 44, at the cell's own x+6, +20, +34 and +50. Cell 0 (no-repeat, 28x20 tile) reads 237,57,57 and 57,177,77 at +6 and +20 on row 12 and white everywhere else - one tile in the top-left quarter. Cell 1 (repeat) reads coloured at all four columns on all three rows, with row 12 red and green and row 44 blue and yellow, which is the tile's own top and bottom halves. Cell 2 (repeat-x) matches cell 1 on row 12 and is white on rows 30 and 44. Cell 3 (repeat-y) is coloured at +6 and +20 on all three rows and white at +34 and +50.
checkable_space_and_round: cells 4 and 5 draw a 15x13 tile in the same 56x40 cell. Cell 4 (space) fits three across with eleven pixels left over, shared as two gaps of five and a half: on row 30 it reads 50,90,230 at +6, then 160,180,250 at +20 - white showing through the gap - then 244,210,50 at +34 and 247,216,56 at +50. Cell 5 (round) scales the tile to fourteen so four fit exactly, and reads the same 92,118,194 at +6, +20 and +34 on row 30: three samples fourteen apart landing at the same point of three different tiles is what an exactly-divided axis looks like.
expected: no-repeat draws one tile at the origin. repeat-x and repeat-y tile one axis each. repeat tiles both. space keeps the tile and shares the remainder out as gaps, pinning the first and last tiles to the edges. round scales the tile until a whole number fits.
why_the_tile_is_drawn_at_a_size: the asset is 8x4. At its own size every cell is a smear a reader cannot check and every sample has to land in the one four-pixel row the tiles occupy - which is how this fixture's first image was written, and it read white in three of six cells because the samples missed the tiles rather than because the tiles were missing. A quarter-cell tile reads as four quadrants.
why_cells_4_and_5_use_a_different_tile: on a box the tile divides evenly, repeat, space and round are the same picture: there is no remainder to share and nothing to round to. A fixture built that way pins three keywords with one picture and passes with all three collapsed into repeat, which is exactly what a pattern-shader implementation would do. The 15x13 tile leaves eleven pixels across and one down.
the_axes_are_read_separately: cells 2 and 3 are the pair that catches a swapped axis. An implementation with x and y crossed draws a picture for both keywords, so a cell against the unrepeated case passes while the two keywords mean each other; only reading repeat-x's white rows against repeat-y's white columns tells them apart.
status: measured from the committed image. Tiling landed in the commit that added this fixture. Any of cells 1 to 5 reading the same picture as another is the regression it exists to catch.
